key_insight: Personalized RewardBench is a benchmark that measures how well reward models capture diverse individual preferences, showing that high aggregate RM scores often mask poor personalization and misalignment with specific users.
problem_solved: Fills the evaluation gap for reward models by providing a systematic way to assess and compare how well RMs align with individual user values instead of only population-level quality.
method: Curated multi-persona dataset: collect prompts/responses annotated with preference labels across a diverse set of realistic user personas.
Per-person evaluation protocol: score responses per persona using pairwise comparisons and direct scoring to compute personalization metrics (per-user rank correlation, calibration, consistency).
Benchmarking suite: standardized tasks, baseline RMs, and diagnostic analyses to surface when models succeed or fail at pluralistic alignment.
impact: Helps researchers and practitioners detect personalization failures, prioritize RM improvements that respect individual values, and benchmark progress toward pluralistic alignment in LLM systems.
visual_elements: Persona mosaic/wheel: icons representing diverse user profiles and preference axes
Bar chart: aggregate RM score vs average per-person RM score to highlight discrepancy
Heatmap or matrix: per-person rank correlations or calibration errors across models and personas
Pipeline diagram: dataset → RM scoring → metric computation → diagnostics
paper_title: Personalized RewardBench: Evaluating Reward Models with Human Aligned Personalization
paper_authors: Qiyao Ma, Dechen Gao, Rui Cai, Boqi Zhao, Hanchu Zhou
